Is Kling AI free?

Edited by Emmanuel Gonzalez

Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

Partly. Official Kling documents fetched Nov 24, 2026, 7:48–7:50 PM ET (4:48–4:50 PM PT) list a Basic plan at $0.00 with no monthly credits, for personal non-commercial use, so this page does not turn a recurring free allowance into a clip count. Kling’s official blog dated Jul 28, 2026 publishes planning figures for paid Standard and 4K credits (see below), which this page does not convert into a VidFare cost per second. If you pay, the cheapest Kling 3.0 rate we track is $0.0225 per second on Higgsfield’s Ultra (annual) plan at 720p, not stated, estimated from credit plan: about $0.1125 for a 5s clip, assuming every credit you pay for is used (checked Nov 24, 2026, using a Higgsfield Black Friday plan price of $45 a month billed yearly that Higgsfield says ends November 25, 2026, 7:00 PM ET (4:00 PM PT)). The next-cheapest catalog row is $0.0263 per second on Higgsfield, Ultra (annual), 1080p (checked Nov 24, 2026). Kling’s own API charges $0.084 per second at 720p without audio, or $0.42 for a 5s clip (checked Nov 24, 2026).

Last checked 2026-11-24. Official static pages were read Nov 24, 2026, 7:48–7:50 PM ET (4:48–4:50 PM PT), without signing in. Catalog rows use the date on each row.

Key takeaways

  • There is a $0 plan in official documents. Basic is $0.00 on Kling’s official llms.txt, with no monthly credits, fetched Nov 24, 2026.
  • Free output is not for commercial use. Official llms.txt describes Basic as personal non-commercial use. The official blog dated Jul 28, 2026 says the same, and lists commercial use and brand watermark removal on Standard.
  • Cheapest official paid plan in those documents. Standard is $6.99 for the first month, then $8.80/month (list $10.00), or $79.20/year (list $120.00), with 660 credits a month, fetched Nov 24, 2026.
  • Cheapest Kling 3.0 per second we track. $0.0225/s on Higgsfield, Ultra (annual), 720p, not stated, estimated from credit plan, checked Nov 24, 2026. It assumes every credit you pay for is used, using a Higgsfield Black Friday plan price of $45 a month billed yearly that Higgsfield says ends November 25, 2026, 7:00 PM ET (4:00 PM PT).
  • No free API tier is listed. The official API is $0.084/s at 720p without audio and $0.126/s with audio, checked Nov 24, 2026.

Is Kling AI free?

Partly. Nov 24, 2026, Kling’s official llms.txt, which cites the membership page as its source, lists a Basic plan at $0 with no monthly credits, for personal non-commercial use. The same reading of that file lists paid Standard, Pro, Premier, and Ultra plans. The official credit-planning blog dated Jul 28, 2026, re-read Nov 24, 2026, also lists Basic at $0 with no monthly credits and says generated content on Basic is not for commercial use. The membership page itself is a JavaScript app and produced no saved payload on this check, so this page does not treat its on-screen wording as confirmed. Sources: Kling’s official llms.txt, fetched Nov 24, 2026, 7:48–7:50 PM ET (4:48–4:50 PM PT), and Kling’s official credit-planning blog, dated Jul 28, 2026.

What does the free Basic plan include?

Official llms.txt, fetched Nov 24, 2026, 7:48–7:50 PM ET (4:48–4:50 PM PT), lists Basic at $0.00 with no monthly credits. Standard, the cheapest official paid plan in that file, is $6.99 for the first month, then $8.80 a month (list $10.00), or $79.20 a year (list $120.00), with 660 credits a month. The official blog dated Jul 28, 2026 lists the same $0 Basic plan, no monthly credits, and element creation quantity 30 on Basic versus 50 on Standard. It lists 1080p video generation, brand watermark removal, image upscaling, video extension, fast-track generation, and commercial use as Standard benefits. Those blog figures are dated Jul 28, 2026; confirm the live membership page before you buy. Sources: Kling’s official llms.txt · Kling’s official credit-planning blog.

    How many free Kling videos can you make?

    Official llms.txt lists no monthly credits on Basic, so this page does not turn a recurring free allowance into a clip count. Kling does publish dated planning figures on its official blog (Jul 28, 2026): Standard’s 660 monthly credits are described as “660 images / 33 720p videos,” and native 4K output for the Kling VIDEO 3.0 series is described as 30 credits per second, as a planning reference to confirm on the live generation panel. This page does not convert those blog figures into a VidFare cost per second, and it does not invent a free-clip count. The same llms.txt file says credit use varies by model, resolution, duration, audio, and generation mode, and that failed generations do not consume credits. Sources: Kling’s official llms.txt, fetched Nov 24, 2026, 7:48–7:50 PM ET (4:48–4:50 PM PT); Kling’s official credit-planning blog, dated Jul 28, 2026.

    Can you use free Kling videos commercially?

    Official llms.txt describes Basic as being for personal non-commercial use, and lists commercial use on Standard. The official blog dated Jul 28, 2026 says generated content on Basic is not for commercial use, and lists commercial use and brand watermark removal as Standard benefits. The Terms of Paid Service and Credits Policy pages are JavaScript apps and produced no saved payload on this check, so this page does not quote them. Sources: Kling’s official llms.txt · Kling’s official credit-planning blog.

    Is the Kling API free?

    No free tier is listed. Kling’s official API pricing document, checked Nov 24, 2026, does not mention free trial units. It bills Kling 3.0 per second of output: $0.084 per second at 720p without native audio and $0.126 per second with native audio. A 5-second 720p clip is $0.42 without audio and $0.63 with audio. These are published rates, not plan estimates. Source: Kling’s official API pricing document.

    What is confirmed, and what is not?

    • Confirmed Nov 24, 2026, 7:48–7:50 PM ET (4:48–4:50 PM PT) in Kling’s official llms.txt: Basic at $0.00 with no monthly credits, for personal non-commercial use; Standard’s first-month, ongoing, list, and yearly prices and 660 credits a month; credits deducted on generation and refunded if a generation fails; standard credit packs at $10 for 660 credits ($1 for 66 credits).
    • Confirmed from Kling’s official credit-planning blog, dated Jul 28, 2026, re-read Nov 24, 2026: Basic at $0 with no monthly credits and no commercial use; element creation 30 vs 50; Standard planning figures of “660 images / 33 720p videos”; 4K planning reference of 30 credits per second for the Kling VIDEO 3.0 series, to confirm on the live generation panel; Standard benefits including 1080p video, brand watermark removal, and commercial use.
    • Confirmed Nov 24, 2026 in Kling’s API pricing document: the Kling 3.0 720p rates above, and no mention of free trial units.
    • Catalog rows: every dollar-per-second figure in the table is a current data/prices.json row, sorted cheapest first, each with its own checked date and source.
    • Not confirmed on this check (no saved membership or policy payload): wording on the JavaScript membership page, including any limited-time sale or a monthly free-credit claim for accounts without a paid plan; the Terms of Paid Service; and the Credits Policy. Those claims are omitted rather than guessed.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page.
